recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7733 unless Pharmacy chooses a new, broader policy change for MedicationAdministration.performer.actor.
issue_request: FHIR-7733 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy issue from the DSTU1 ballot asking how to document a patient or someone other than a practitioner administering medication. The approved resolution was to expand what the former MedicationAdministration.practitioner element could point to, including patient/agent-style performers, and update the definition to discuss the performer of the administration.
initial_application: Commit b11981d13acc78914bac8350efcaa2654cda7848 applied the direct DSTU-era change by changing MedicationAdministration.practitioner from Reference(Practitioner) to Reference(Practitioner | Patient | RelatedPerson) in the spreadsheet source. Later event-model harmonization in 7003eba639b96a6cb1198300f293effe3f4bda1d moved that concept into MedicationAdministration.performer.actor while retaining Patient and RelatedPerson and adding Device.
additional_context: MedicationAdministration is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current rename table maps the old MedicationAdministration.practitioner name to MedicationAdministration.performer. Current StructureDefinition XML defines performer as who or what performed the administration, and performer.actor accepts Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, RelatedPerson, Device, and Group. Later FHIR-37631 device-performer clarification is already represented on the combined branch and does not conflict with this decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active authoritative source already conveys the requested patient/non-practitioner performer scope and performer semantics.

related_jiras.note: Clarified when a device is a MedicationAdministration performer versus merely used in administration; it supports preserving the current performer/device distinction and is already represented on the combined branch.
